strategies.overview: Gallade is a very threatening wallbreaker that uses its Sharpness-boosted offensive coverage options to threaten big damage on most of the metagame. It can notably 2HKO walls like Hippowdon, Slowbro, and Chesnaught, making it an excellent tool at dealing with defensive teams in particular, as nothing can reliably take its hits. It is, however, held back by its average bulk. While its special bulk can let it tank some pretty big hits like Gengar's Shadow Ball, Armarouge's Armor Cannon, and Magnezone's Discharge, its physical bulk is terrible, and it will have trouble taking hits it doesn't resist from any mildly threatening foes such as Bisharp's Sucker Punch and Mamoswine's Earthquake. Its biggest weakness is its mediocre Speed leaving it vulnerable to revenge killing attempts from faster threats like Krookodile, Gardevoir, and Noivern; Choice Scarf users such as Gardevoir; and priority users like Mimikyu and Bisharp. It therefore struggles against more offensive teams containing more of these fast threats.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Knock Off or Night Slash can be used over Leaf Blade to hit bulky Psychic-types, notably Armarouge, harder. Night Slash has consistently high damage and good synergy with Scope Lens thanks to its higher critical chance. Knock Off hits for slightly less and only gets its boosted Base Power once, resulting in it being less effective against the likes of Slowbro, Reuniclus, and Cresselia, but it has the upside of removing items like Rocky Helmet and Heavy-Duty Boots.

Checks and Counters

Armarouge: Armarouge's good bulk, unique typing that resists both of Gallade's STAB moves and Leaf Blade, high damage, and Weak Armor ability make it an effective check that can use Gallade as setup fodder.

Faster Wallbreakers: Faster wallbreakers like Gardevoir and Maushold can threaten Gallade prior to it using Agility, while Choice Scarf users like Gengar are still faster than +2 Gallade.

Priority Users: As a setup sweeper with mediocre Defense, Gallade is especially weak to priority moves; it's weak to Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak and neutral to Sucker Punch and Aqua Jet from the likes of Crawdaunt and Bisharp, which can easily revenge kill it. While Extreme Speed from Entei hits it hard, it can, in a pinch, use Tera Steel to take less damage.

movesets.name: Setup Sweeper
movesets.description:
Set Details

Gallade has a unique niche in being a wallbreaker that threatens a 2HKO on the main physical walls of the tier such as Chesnaught and Slowbro. Psycho Cut not making contact comes in handy against Rocky Helmet users and Flame Body Pokemon, like Hippowdon and Talonflame. Leaf Blade is useful coverage for hitting bulky Water- and Ground-types that could wall Gallade otherwise such as Slowbro and Hippowdon. With Swords Dance, Gallade gets the opportunity to OHKO most physical walls in the tier like Chesnaught, Hippowdon, and Slowbro, while Agility allows it to outspeed foes that would normally revenge kill it like Gengar and Gardevoir. Lum Berry allows it to shrug off status effects that can be inflicted by Slowbro, Talonflame, and Quagsire; it works best on Swords Dance sets, as they don't need more damage. Life Orb is an alternative that fits the most on Agility variants, as it adds damage that can be lacking, letting them OHKO some notable threats like Gardevoir after Stealth Rock. Scope Lens is another option to get additional damage on Agility sets; it is less reliable than Life Orb but crucially doesn't cause recoil, which can help Gallade to tank important hits such as Earthquake from Krookodile and Shadow Sneak from Mimikyu. It can also let Gallade break through Terastilized Iron Defense setup sweepers such as Tera Ghost Registeel. Tera Steel is at its best on Swords Dance sets, letting Gallade sponge hits from Fairy-types such as Gardevoir and Diancie extremely well while neutering some of its original weaknesses. Since Agility sets have less issue with these threats and much prefer an offensive item over Lum Berry, Tera Fire is preferred to absorb burns from Talonflame.

Gallade is a huge threat on Sticky Web and bulky offense teams, as it's able to dig holes in the opponent's defensive structure and can take advantage of paralysis and Sticky Web to fix its speed issue. Because of its average bulk, it also loves pivots, thus working well with allies such as Jirachi, Raikou, and Mienshao; Jirachi can also spread paralysis to allow it to outpace foes like Mienshao and Gardevoir. Raikou likes Gallade being able to threaten the common Ground-types that can KO it, and Mienshao benefits from Gallade's wallbreaking potential, helping it find an opening to clean a weakened team. However, they're all weak to Armarouge, so priority moves from the likes of Entei and Bisharp or bulky allies that resist Armor Cannon such as Diancie, Noivern, and Cyclizar may be needed. On teams utilizing Ribombee's Sticky Web, Gallade will need to be heavily supported, as it is quite weak to some already difficult foes to deal with for Sticky Web teams like Bisharp, and Armarouge. One particularly great ally is Low Kick Bisharp, which can consistently beat opposing Bisharp and revenge kill Armarouge. Calm Mind + Heavy-Duty Boots Armarouge is a great Mienshao revenge killer, as it can survive a hit and enable Weak Armor while also being a threatening sweeper on its own; it may also force a special wall in, which is perfect to give Gallade an opportunity to set up. Teams stacking multiple physical setup sweepers such as Bisharp, Mimikyu, and Maushold appreciate Swords Dance Gallade's ability to help wear down shared checks like Quagsire and Hippowdon. Agility Gallade benefits most from other wallbreakers like Entei, Crawdaunt, and Breloom thanks to their ability to weaken physical walls, letting it clean a weakened team. After using Agility, it can outspeed most Choice Scarf users aside from Gengar, helping it clean teams relying on the likes of Mienshao and Gardevoir for speed control. Entry hazard support such as Stealth Rock or Spikes can help greatly with putting foes such as Gardevoir or Armarouge in KO range of Gallade's attacks.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Set Details

Choice Band Gallade can act as an extremely powerful wallbreaker with its Sharpness-boosted STAB moves. Leaf Blade targets Water- and Ground-types like Slowbro and Hippowdon. Knock Off provides utility by removing items from possible switch-ins like Hippowdon and Slowbro, and it hits Psychic-types like Reuniclus and Cresselia. Shadow Sneak lets it revenge kill weakened Armarouge, Gengar, and Choice Scarf Gardevoir. Trick can cripple walls like Reuniclus, and removing Gallade's Choice item can help ease prediction against teams with multiple Pokemon resistant to its STAB moves. Tera Steel lets it flip the matchup against Flying- and Fairy-types like Noivern and Gardevoir, while Tera Dark boosts Knock Off, guaranteeing a 2HKO on Slowbro; helps answer Ghost-types like Gengar as well as Psychic-types; and provides a resistance to Bisharp's Sucker Punch.

Choice Band Gallade often finds itself on balance and bulky offense teams that can patch up its physical frailty and mediocre Speed while appreciating its ability to punch holes through defensive cores. Cleaners like Hisuian Lilligant, Maushold, and Armarouge can sweep teams after Gallade has weakened shared checks like Hippowdon and Slowbro. Due to Gallade having the coverage to 2HKO any Pokemon in the tier, no slower Pokemon want to stay in on it, letting it effectively force switches; this synergizes well with entry hazard setters such as Hippowdon, Klefki, and Krookodile, since their hazards can help chip down the opposing team and make Gallade less reliant on prediction. If Gallade is running Shadow Sneak over Knock Off, answers to bulky Psychic-types such as Slowbro and Reuniclus are necessary. Bisharp and Encore Jirachi can help alleviate this weakness. Pivots like Cyclizar and Raikou can help bring Gallade onto the field safely after inviting in Umbreon and Hisuian Goodra. Paralysis support from the likes of Jirachi, Slowbro, and Klefki can make Gallade a terrifying foe by crippling its faster checks, like Talonflame and Suicune, making them unable to outspeed it. Gallade should be paired with defensive Pokemon like Slowbro, Empoleon, and Umbreon that can switch into revenge kill attempts from the likes of Noivern and Talonflame.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Set Details

Choice Scarf Gallade is a strong revenge killer and late-game cleaner with good utility. Leaf Blade lets it revenge kill Water-types like Feraligatr and hit Pokemon like Hippowdon. Knock Off lets it hit Psychic-types like Armarouge and Reuniclus as well as removes items from defensive checks like Slowbro. Trick can cripple walls such as Suicune, Cresselia, and Calm Mind Reuniclus. Tera Steel changes Gallade's Fairy and Flying weaknesses into resistances, which helps it tank hits from Gardevoir and Noivern. Tera Dark boosts Knock Off damage, guaranteeing a 2HKO on Reuniclus as well as providing a very high chance to OHKO Armarouge, and it gives Galladea resistance to Ghost- and Dark-type attacks from Pokemon like Gengar and Bisharp.

Choice Scarf Gallade performs best on balance and bulky offense structures, as they can help weaken its checks. Stealth Rock users like Hippowdon can help weaken Gallade's checks throughout the match to allow it to eventually clean late-game,and it can switch into Pokemon that threaten Gallade out like Choice Scarf Mienshao and Mimikyu; Spikes setters like Chesnaught and Gastrodon can fulfill a similar role. These Pokemon appreciate Gallade's Knock Off support to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from the opposing team. Wallbreakers such as Krookodile and Entei can help weaken physical walls that Gallade struggles with such as Reuniclus and Hippowdon. Armarouge answers like Umbreon and Hisuian Goodra are necessary, as Armarouge can use Gallade as setup fodder if it locks into an attack that Armarouge resists. Gallade appreciates pivot support and hazard removal from the likes of Jirachi and Cyclizar, allowing it to enter the field easily and leverage its useful special bulk more consistently.

movesets.name: Assault Vest (Fighting)
movesets.description:
Gallade offers incredible value to Fighting teams due to its Sharpness ability, access to a variety of slicing moves, and Assault Vest complementing its natural specially defensive bulk, giving the invaluable utility to beat threatening Psychic-type Pokemon such as Latios and Choice Specs Greninja. Psycho Cut is able to help combat a plethora of Poison-type Pokemon that annoy Fighting teams such as Galarian Weezing, Toxapex, and Amoonguss. Sacred Sword complements Psycho Cut by threatening Dark-type Pokemon that attempt to switch-in while also having the incredible ability to ignore Defense raises such as Archaludon's Stamina and Iron Defense Skarmory. Night Slash is another boosted coverage option that deals with threatening Psychic- and Ghost-type Pokemon such as the aforementioned Latias, Gholdengo, and Sinistcha. Knock Off is a possible alternative that provides the utility of removing items such as Rocky Helmet and Heavy Duty Boots but lacks the consistent damage output of Night Slash. Shadow Sneak complements Night Slash and Knock Off by being useful priority that can threaten and revenge kill fast Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokemon such as Flutter Mane, Dragapult, Iron Boulder. 96 Speed EVs enables Gallade to outspeed Modest Magnezone while the given investment in HP and Special Defense in tandem with Assault Vest, allowing Gallade to survive an attack from Choice Specs Flutter Mane in order to OHKO it back with Psycho Cut, alleviating pressure on Fighting teams.

Iron Valiant is an essential teammate for Gallade, being able to remove troublesome Dark-type Pokemon such as Sableye and Mandibuzz. Great Tusk is another incredible teammate, providing a defensive switch-in for physical attackers that could otherwise overwhelm Gallade such as Excadrill, Ceruledge, and Dragonite. Great Tusk also has the utility of removing entry hazards, which could otherwise hinder Gallade. Sneasler complements Gallade by removing Fairy-type Pokemon such as Enamorus, Hatterene, Primarina, and Iron Valiant. Sneasler also has utility in crippling set up Pokemon with Switcheroo, spreading status via Poison Touch and Dire Claw and pivoting with U-turn so that Gallade can enter the battlefield at the most opportune times. Keldeo is an incredible teammate that complements Gallade by removing physical walls such as Hippowdon, Skeledirge, and Gliscor. Iron Hands is a useful teammate, being able to sponge Flying-type STAB coverage from Pokemon such as Galarian Zapdos, Galarian Moltres, and Tornadus-T. Breloom is another option that helps Gallade by inflicting sleep, crippling troublesome foes such as Skeledirge and Torkoal, as well as putting offensive pressure on physical walls such as Slowbro and Quagsire. Similarly, Hisuian Lilligant is a physical sweeper that thrives on Gallade's ability to remove its checks in Pokemon such as Latias, Greninja, and Volcarona. Galarian Zapdos offers a Ground-immune Pokemon to add aditional protection from threats such as Excadrill and Great Tusk.

strategies.overview:
This Pokemon has been updated to reflect Regulation H, that lasts until January 5h, 2025. After this, Regulation G will return.

movesets.name: All-out Attacker
movesets.description:
• With its wide range of moveset options and its offense-boosting ability Sharpness, Gallade is excellent at dueling a wide variety of threats. Especially notable is Scared Sword, letting Gallade ignore Stamina Archaludon's accumulated boosts.

  • Night Slash versus Knock Off: Night Slash's consistent power is best for pure offense, potentially 2HKOing targets like Bold Gholdengo, assuming they can't stall with Recover and Rocky Helmet. If more utility is desired, Knock Off can be used for removing opposing items.

  • Shadow Sneak: Shadow Sneak Gallade's most consistent as a priority move, dealing good damage to targets like Gholdengo and Mimikyu.

  • Leaf Blade: Leaf Blade OHKOes Primarina and is Gallade's best hope of muscling past Dondozo.

  • Triple Axel: Though it suffers from some reliability issues, Triple Axel makes Dragonite rue the day it didn't Terastallize against Gallade!

Other Options

  • Aqua Cutter: Aqua Cutter benefits from Sharpness, but it doesn't add a lot of extra coverage.

  • Feint: Feint lets Gallade pick off weakened Dragonite before they can launch Extreme Speed, but otherwise hitting Gholdengo with Shadow Sneak is usually more useful.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Gallade uses Focus Sash or Assault Vest as its main tool for cushioning a big hit and has great natural coverage. Therefore, Tera is reserved mostly for emergency situations.

  • Fire: Beyond offering a useful Fairy-type resistance, Tera Fire blocks Volcarona from burning Gallade.

  • Dark: Tera Dark not only boosts Night Slash and Knock Off, but provides a key Ghost-type resistance against Gholdengo.

  • Steel: Tera Steel flips Gallade's weakness to Fairy-type attacks to a resistance. The Ice resistance can also be used in a pinch to keep Baxcalibur's Icicle Spear from OHKOing Gallade through Focus Sash.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost's immunity to Normal- and Fighting-type moves can thwart revenge kill attempts from Mach Punch users and Extreme Speed Dragonite, giving Gallade an opportunity to break Multiscale on the latter.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Gallade has enough Special Defense to make good use of Assault Vest, which lets it survive Tera Normal Ursaluna-B. Compared to Focus Sash, Assault Vest isn't rendered useless by Stealth Rock chip, making Gallade a safer mid- or late-game option.

  • Focus Sash: With Focus Sash, Gallade duels opposing Focus Sash users with its hard-hitting STAB attacks and priority moves, letting it focus on Speed investment.

  • Scope Lens: While Scope Lens is risky due to Gallade's average bulk and Speed, it pairs well with the increased critical hit ratio many of Gallade's attacks have.

EV Spreads

  • 140 HP / 244 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 116 Spe with Adamant: This spread is to be used with Assault Vest, surviving Silk Scarf Tera Normal Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon and Vacuum Wave together, while outspeeding even Timid Ursaluna-B and Jolly Ursaluna.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: A maximum offense spread is standard for Focus Sash and Speed ties with offensive Adamant Dragonite. Jolly can be used to get the jump on Modest Archaludon, especially if using Shadow Sneak to stop Sturdy variants from activating Custap Berry in time.

  • 236 HP / 244 Atk / 28 SpD with Adamant: Sacrificing Speed for bulk lets Assault Vest Gallade survive Life Orb Tera Normal Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon followed by Vacuum Wave.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
• With Choice Scarf, Gallade is a decent anti-lead against several early-game setups and an unexpected revenge killer.

  • Knock Off versus Night Slash: Knock Off remains a strong disruption move with or without Trick, provided you exercise caution if you've already used Trick. Night Slash has more offensive presence than Knock Off and is a good choice if you really need to hit Gholdengo with consistent damage.

  • Triple Axel versus Leaf Blade: Triple Axel makes Gallade a surprising revenge killer against Garchomp and severely punishes Dragonite that don't Terastallize. Leaf Blade helps against more defensive foes, being a great coverage option for slashing through Primarina and being your best move against Dondozo.

  • Trick: Trick with Choice Scarf lets Gallade permanently cripple setup Pokemon like Annihilape and Garganacl.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Choice Scarf Gallade normally isn't a strong user of Tera. It is best used in situations where Gallade already has momentum and needs to preserve it.

  • Fire: Tera Fire makes facing down Volcarona far less risky thanks to the burn immunity, as well as providing a useful Fairy-type resistance.

  • Steel: Tera Steel provides a welcome resistance to Fairy-type attacks and Dragonite's Extreme Speed.

  • Dark: Tera Dark stops Choice Scarf Gholdengo from revenge killing with Shadow Ball, while boosting Night Slash and Knock Off

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost grants immunity to Extreme Speed and Mach Punch, letting Gallade keep its speed advantage against Dragonite and Breloom even when its low on health.

  • Grass: Tera Grass can surprise Spore users like Breloom, letting Gallade score an easy KO or cripple them with Trick. Leaf Blade also becomes a 2HKO against Dondozo.

strategies.overview:
• Gallade is a strong option on Trick Room teams thanks to its high physical damage output, unique coverage and utility movepool. It can deal with many problematic matchups for Trick Room, such as set up sweepers via Sacred Sword and spread moves via Wide Guard.

  • Gallade is used on teams with Indeedee-F, as the Fighting-type coverage it provides is crucial in dealing with Incineroar, Ting-Lu and other Dark-types that give Trick Room sweepers such as Hatterene trouble. Sharpness-boosted Sacred Sword does massive damage, putting pressure on opponents from turn one, as well as checking several problematic matchups, such as Dondozo. Wide Guard removes the most common way to bypass Indeedee-F's Follow Me, spread moves, and presents mind games on opponents on whether Gallade will use Wide Guard or set up Trick Room.

  • Gallade's typing is amazing offensively, but defensively leaves much to be desired. Its Defense and HP are low, making it vulnerable to attackers like Rillaboom and Urshifu that can take one attack from Gallade while OHKOing it back. While its Special Defense is high, it is made moot by relevant special attackers such as Flutter Mane and Tornadus, which both resist Sacred Sword and hit it for super effective damage. However, it should be noted that Wide Guard blocks both Bleakwind Storm and Dazzling Gleam.

movesets.name: Trick Room Abuser
movesets.description:
• Psycho Cut and Sacred Sword are the highest base power moves that take advantage of Sharpness.

  • The Defense EVs allow Gallade to survive a Wicked Blow and Surging Strikes from Urshifu-S and Urshifu-R, respectively.

  • Tera Grass allows Gallade to ignore powder moves from Amoonguss, a common Trick Room counter, and resist common physical attackers such as Rillaboom. Alternatively, Tera Fire can be used to resist common anti-Trick Room leads such as Chi-Yu and Flutter Mane, as well as giving Gallade a Fairy resist.

strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Gallade isn't a particularly bulky Pokemon, so it is often paired with partners more capable of setting up Trick Room while Gallade threatens foes that threaten its partners. Gallade also can be paired with redirection that allows it to set up Trick Room.
  • Hatterene pairs well with Gallade, as it is more capable of setting Trick Room up thanks to its bulk, while Gallade threatens foes such as Incineroar and Kingambit that Hatterene struggles to damage in return. Hatterene additionally threatens physically defensive foes that Gallade struggles to OHKO such as Amoonguss and provides powerful spread damage with Dazzling Gleam, which complements Gallade when it fails to achieve an OHKO. Indeedee-F provides redirection, allowing Gallade to safely set up Trick Room. It is additionally capable of setting up Trick Room itself while Gallade provides Wide Guard support. Indeedee-F setting up Psychic Terrain further supports Gallade by preventing Fake Out disruption and increasing the damage of Psycho Cut.
  • Amoonguss threatens to put Gallade to sleep with Spore, often forcing it to Terastallize into a Grass-type. A partner Torkoal threatens Amoonguss with Eruption and Weather Ball and outspeeds it while Trick Room is active. Gholdengo is difficult for Gallade to remove and threatens to deal significant damage with its STAB attacks. Torkoal and Ursaluna can survive Gholdengo's attacks and threaten it in return with Eruption and Headlong Rush. Basculegion-M threatens Gallade with its STAB attacks, so a partner Kingambit is capable of surviving these attacks and threatening it with Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave.

Strategy Comments

  • Gallade is a sweeper and a support Pokemon for Trick Room teams. It performs best early-game by removing threats preventing Trick Room from being set up or setting up Trick Room itself.
  • Gallade should always be led with a partner capable of setting Trick Room such as Hatterene or Indeedee-F. If paired with Hatterene, Gallade can be used to remove threats such as Kingambit and Incineroar. When facing Gholdengo, it can use Wide Guard to protect Hatterene from Make It Rain. If Gallade is paired with Indeedee-F, it can set Trick Room as Indeedee-F redirects attacks with Follow Me. However, there may be situations where Indeedee-F can be used to set up Trick Room itself while Gallade removes an opposing threat like Kingambit. Gallade can also use Wide Guard while Indeedee-F sets up Trick Room, protecting both Pokemon from attacks like Eruption from Hisuian Typhlosion.
  • Gallade is checked by Ghost-types and threatened by their attacks like Shadow Ball and Last Respects. As a result, Gallade is very reliant on redirection from Indeedee-F or switching to it if Indeedee-F is not lead. Gallade also relies on Kingambit to threaten them.
  • Foes with Imprison like Indeedee-M disrupt Trick Room teams and are often difficult for Gallade to remove, so it relies on partners like Ursaluna and Kingambit for this. If the opponent pivots around to stall out Trick Room turns, getting KOs while Trick Room is active becomes difficult for Gallade and its partners. To mitigate this, overwhelming the foes with powerful attacks from teammates like Ursaluna helps to reduce the effectiveness of the switches.

movesets.name: Offensive Trick Room Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Gallade is an offensive threat thanks to Sharpness and its ability to set Trick Room up for itself and its partners.
  • Sacred Sword ignores the Defense boosts of foes like Archaludon and Dondozo. Psycho Cut is used as a consistent Psychic-type STAB move that is also boosted by Sharpness. Its damage can be boosted further by a partner's Psychic Terrain. Wide Guard protects Gallade and its partner from spread attacks such as Make It Rain and Eruption.
  • Clear Amulet prevents Gallade's Attack from being hindered by Intimidate and Parting Shot, allowing it to always deal threatening damage to metagame staples such as Incineroar.
  • Tera Grass provides Gallade with an immunity to Spore, Sleep Powder, and Rage Powder while allowing it to resist Electro Shot from Archaludon. Tera Fire, unlike Tera Grass, removes Gallade's weakness to Flying-type attacks such as Hurricane from Pelipper without gaining a weakness to Poison-type attacks such as Dire Claw from Sneasler, and it also allows Gallade to resist Make It Rain from Gholdengo. Tera Fire additionally provides an immunity to burn.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 7-8 points

Overview: A great ability in Sharpness and a fantastic pool of coverage moves allow Gallade to offensively threaten most foes. Unfortunately, it's generally unable to blow through opposing teams due to its middling Speed and poor physical bulk. Gallade is able to alleviate some of these problems through its solid setup and utility options, but it often wants to run more than four moves, which makes it difficult to fit on a team along with its other shortcomings.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Setup Sweeper: Gallade has multiple threatening setup options including Swords Dance, Agility, and Bulk Up. It can also utilize its solid utility moves to disrupt opposing walls, giving itself more opportunities to set up.

Wallbreaker: Gallade's strong STAB moves and coverage allows it to offensively threaten most Pokemon. Foes attempting to wall it must not only be wary of its coverage but also its disruptive utility moves like Taunt, Encore, and Trick.

Revenge Killer: With a Choice Scarf and great coverage options, Gallade can revenge kill most Pokemon or use Trick to disrupt an opposing wall. However, its middling Speed unfortunately means it cannot outspeed most foes that have boosted their own Speed.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Sacred Sword, Psycho Cut

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Agility, Bulk Up

Utility Moves: Trick, Taunt, Encore, Substitute, Destiny Bond, Brick Break, Will-O-Wisp, Thunder Wave

Coverage: Triple Axel, Knock Off, Night Slash, Leaf Blade, Aqua Cutter, Earthquake, X-Scissor, Poison Jab, Shadow Sneak, Thunder Punch, Fire Punch, Aerial Ace, Stone Edge, Shadow Claw

Niche Moves

Teleport: Teleport can be used to slow pivot, working well on sets with Choice Scarf or Choice Band.

Light Screen / Reflect: When Gallade is unable to achieve much offensively, dual screens can be used to help support its partners.

Common Items

Damage-boosting Items: The damage boost and ability to change moves from damage-boosting items like Life Orb, Expert Belt, and Black Belt are all greatly appreciated on most Gallade sets.

Choice Scarf: To get around its middling Speed, Gallade can use Choice Scarf and its great coverage moves to become a solid revenge killer. Trick can also be used to cripple opposing walls.

Niche Items

Lum Berry: Lum Berry can give Gallade an opportunity to set up against foes with otherwise devastating status moves.

Assault Vest: Combined with its solid Special Defense, Assault Vest provides Gallade with respectable special bulk while allowing it to utilize its plethora of coverage moves.

Choice Band: If immediate power is needed, Choice Band is a solid choice to break down defensive walls. This can also be paired with Trick to cripple opposing walls.

Scope Lens: Scope Lens combined with Sharpness-boosted high-critical hit ratio moves including Psycho Cut, Leaf Blade, and Night Slash gives Gallade the opportunity to land a critical hit 50% of the time.

Focus Sash: To get around its frailty, Focus Sash can be used to guarantee damage or cripple a particularly threatening foe with a status effect.

Resistance Berries: Roseli Berry, Coba Berry, and Kasib Berry can let Gallade survive super effective hits, allowing it to set up or throw off a strong attack.

Tera

Gallade is not a great option as a secondary Tera Captain compared to other Pokemon at a similar price, since it already has great coverage and does not get much value out of defensive types because of its frailty. If it is a Tera Captain, Tera Fighting and Psychic can be used to boost its STAB types, and it can boost one of its strong coverage options with types such as Tera Ice, Grass, and Dark.

Draft Strategy

Gallade is in an awkward position of not providing defensive utility while not bringing much to the table offensively in certain matchups. This means that it should generally only be on teams that already have strong role compression and other offensive pressure.

Role Compression: Due to only providing offensive pressure, Gallade's partners should are able to work in many roles, especially the utility and defensive roles that it cannot. Partners that can fulfill multiple roles in a draft like Garchomp, Terapagos, and Landorus-T can allow a more one-dimensional Pokemon like Gallade to work.

Strong Offensive Teammates: Although generally threatening, Gallade often doesn't place much pressure on opposing teams. Strong Pokemon like Zarude, Roaring Moon, and Enamorus should be the focal point of a draft's offense.

Faster Partners: Gallade's middling Speed holds it back from achieving much, even with a Choice Scarf or Agility boost. Speedy Pokemon such as Tornadus-T, Meowscarada, and Greninja are able to deal with faster threats that it is unable to handle.

Pivots: Gallade is quite frail, especially on the physical side. By pairing it with partners that can pivot like Scizor, Rotom-W, and Zapdos, it can be the most threatening by switching in safely.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: Psychic-types resist both of Gallade's STAB types making them difficult for it to break. Even with strong coverage moves, foes like Latias, Uxie, and Necrozma can often shut it down.

Faster Pokemon: Without a Choice Scarf or Agility boost, Gallade can be easily be taken advantage of by faster foes such as Palafin. Many Pokemon can also outspeed Choice Scarf sets, including Booster Energy users such as Iron Valiant and Roaring Moon and Choice Scarf users.

Fairy-types: Although Fairy-types do not resist Psycho Cut, Gallade still struggles to break through them due to having worse coverage moves for them. Foes like Tinkaton, Scream Tail, and Hatterene can take a hit and threaten it back with super effective STAB move or status effects.

Status Effects: Gallade absolutely hates being statused. Burn greatly hinders its damage, paralysis allows most foes to outspeed and threaten it, and being poisoned puts it on a timer, which can prevent a sweep.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Fighting)
movesets.description: For Fighting teams, Mega Gallade is one of the best choices, courtesy of its incredible offensive power, typing, and Speed, being the best counter to Fighting's biggest roadblock, Toxapex. Swords Dance increases Mega Gallade's power to the maximum, letting it freely overpower the likes of Mandibuzz and Celesteela. Zen Headbutt beautifully complements a Fighting-type STAB move, as it lets Mega Gallade easily break through any opposing Poison-types that may be annoying walls such as Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Clodsire. Knock Off is another tool in Mega Gallade's arsenal, which lets it take care of Psychic- and Ghost-types—such as Gholdengo, Slowbro, and Aegislash—and wears down Celesteela into range of Close Combat finishing it off. Triple Axel is another option to easily take care of Flying-types such as Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Enamorus. Shadow Sneak can also be considered to pick off faster weakened threats such as Gengar, Choice Scarf Blacephalon, and Mega Alakazam. With all its benefits, Mega Gallade has a few checks in Skeledirge and defensive Gholdengo; hence, offensive Great Tusk and Urshifu-R are great partners in helping take these down. Defensive Great Tusk also helps in setting and removing entry hazards, which is appreciated by Mega Gallade. Mega Gallade is also easily revenge killed by faster offensive threats such as Tornadus-T and Choice Scarf Blacephalon, so Assault Vest Iron Hands is a good check to stop these in their tracks and deal good damage back while also being able to pivot in Mega Gallade with Volt Switch. Breloom and Lilligant-H also helps significantly in the Water matchup against the likes of Mega Swampert and Barraskewda; they can also put opposing foes to sleep to make Gallade's setup easier. Choice Scarf Sneasler helps in the Fairy matchup against the likes of Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko while also being able to set and absorb Toxic Spikes and can U-Turn to pivot in Mega Gallade safely. Iron Valiant is also an amazing partner in the form of a specially offensive threat, complementing Mega Gallade, as it can easily take care of Mega Sableye. Choice Scarf Iron Valiant also outspeeds Mega Swampert under rain and Regieleki under Electric Terrain, making it a great revenge killer if Mega Gallade gets knocked out.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Psychic)
movesets.description: Mega Gallade is a potent wallbreaker on Psychic teams thanks to its greatly appreciated Dark neutrality and good coverage in Knock Off and Triple Axel. Swords Dance allows Mega Gallade to grab a boost on a forced switch and potentially win the game with its high base Speed and astronomical Attack after one boost. Knock Off is crucial to hit opposing Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Slowbro and Gholdengo that would otherwise wall this set, and its item removal is always handy in breaking defensive teams reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots down with Stealth Rock damage and removing key items from Celesteela and Toxapex. Finally, Zen Headbutt does massive work against Poison teams after a single Swords Dance and deals high amounts of damage to Fighting-resistant Pokemon such as Buzzwole and Toxapex. Triple Axel is another alternative, allowing Mega Gallade to hit Flying- and Dragon-types such as Landorus-T and Garchomp. Shadow Sneak can allow Mega Gallade to outspeed and take out Ghost-types such as Choice Scarf Gholdengo and Choice Scarf Blacephalon that could otherwise beat it. Tapu Lele forms a wallbreaking core with Mega Gallade, as they both threaten common checks to each other. Tapu Lele beats Mega Sableye with Moonblast, while Mega Gallade crushes Steel-types such as Heatran and Celesteela that trouble Tapu Lele with Close Combat. Jirachi can take Fairy-type attacks such as Tapu Lele's Moonblast aimed for Mega Gallade, as well as paralyze threats and beat them down with Thunder Wave and Serene Grace-boosted Iron Head, letting Mega Gallade break through them with a timely paralysis. Finally, Jirachi provides Stealth Rock support and a safe pivot in with U-turn. Victini provides speed control with Choice Scarf and defeats Steel-types such as Choice Scarf Gholdengo that Mega Gallade is forced out by while appreciating Mega Gallade's ability to pound Heatran to dust. Deoxys-S provides entry hazard and dual screens support, which Mega Gallade can take advantage of with Knock Off and Swords Dance to break through bulkier teams. Slowbro provides crucial momentum with Teleport while also being able to annoy teams with Scald burns and Future Sight and switch in repeatedly through Regenerator. Celebi can break through troubling physical walls such as Hippowdon and Dondozo that Mega Gallade struggles to make progress against. Finally, Choice Scarf Latias can both remove entry hazards with Defog and use Healing Wish to give Mega Gallade a second chance to break through the opposing team.
